minutes.headline: Sewer Commission put off any recommendation on extending sewer to 5 Chestnut Street until an April 29 meeting.
minutes.summary: The commission heard a developer's request for support to extend the sewer district to 5 Chestnut Street for a roughly 40-unit mixed residential development. A resident objected, citing the commission's own regulations. Members mostly wanted Town Meeting to decide, but voted to wait for town counsel's opinion and move the meeting to April 29. The commission also covered a pump-station control panel replacement, the well policy, the Fitchburg ordinance draft and the FY21 budget.

public_comment.topic: A resident opposed extending the sewer district to all of 5 Chestnut Street, citing the wastewater plan, the 330 gallons per day per 50 feet of frontage rule, and capacity questions.
The same resident said approval would be a special exemption from the commission's own regulations, and that 152 feet of frontage allows only three units.
The resident asked that town counsel be asked whether the parcel would get the proposed flow or only the frontage-based allowance.
A resident announced Earth Day week cleanup projects, with DPW supplying bags and sign-up on the MyRec page.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission put off any recommendation on extending sewer service to 5 Chestnut Street until a special meeting on April 29, to get town counsel's opinion.
Members first moved to leave the 5 Chestnut Street article to Town Meeting, then voted to wait for counsel; the outcome of both votes was not audible.
A resident said approving the extension would be a special exemption from the commission's own frontage-based regulations, and asked that counsel address it.
A motion to approve control panel work at the Electric Ave pump station, contingent on staff sign-off, was made; the outcome was not audible.
The Fitchburg ordinance draft will go to town counsel before it is sent to Fitchburg, and staff were asked to draft a well policy with a meter option.

why_it_matters: Whether the sewer district grows to cover a roughly 40-unit development on Chestnut Street bears on sewer capacity and on whether the commission's frontage rule applies as written, and Town Meeting voters may be asked to decide it.
Pump station repairs and possible overruns in Fitchburg charges are costs the sewer system must cover, so they can affect what ratepayers are billed.
watch_next: Special Sewer Commission meeting on April 29, replacing April 27, for town counsel's opinion on 5 Chestnut Street.
Town counsel's review of the Fitchburg ordinance draft before it goes to Fitchburg.
